analysis: The only change in this PR is a documentation addition to docs/developer/test.md (head lines 1044-1085): a new 'Cluster Pair Coordinated Update' section describing ClusterPairUpdateTests, ClusterServiceUpdateTests and the ClusterSupervisionChecks runner, plus a test command that sets CFFIXED_USER_HOME to a temporary directory. No code, workflow, key handling, attestation, wire or storage behavior changes. I examined the full supplied head text of both units (lines 921-1837) against the threat model. The new section is test guidance only. It states that the checks use loopback and temporary roots, a mock coordinator, and injected or scripted binaries. It does not claim signed-release, launchd, coordinator-routing or hardware qualification, so it does not overclaim assurance on T-043 (watchdog and rollback authority), T-054 or T-057. It does say that a start-check failure rolls back and quarantines the candidate, and that a restored predecessor that cannot start is not re-executed into. That is described as tested behavior, not a new control. The warning to keep CFFIXED_USER_HOME on serving Macs reduces the risk of test runs touching real ~/.darkbloom cluster files. The rest of the file (App Attest dispatch, native qualification, release lanes, prefix-cache and SSD budget tests) is unchanged context. It consistently separates fixture evidence from physical and Apple evidence. Unverified: the described update, rollback and start-check code lives in other files outside this batch, such as ClusterPairUpdate and the supervisor. The docs claims about their behavior, such as pair-coordinated install, partner-gating and the rollback logic, cannot be confirmed here, and any threat-model implications for T-043 and T-061 would belong to the PR that changes that code. No security regression is identified in this documentation-only change.
